findings.issue: audit.lock_chain now sets lock_timeout to 0 while it waits on the tenant advisory lock (lines 187–189). As a result, same-tenant audit-chain contention is bounded only by statement_timeout (the command deadlineMs) and deadlock detection, no longer by lockTimeoutMs. This is the intended semantics. The key reservation stays bounded because the prior value is read in DECLARE and restored as a transaction-local setting. An error while waiting aborts the transaction or subtransaction, and that rolls back the GUC change. RLS, grants, FORCE RLS and SECURITY DEFINER search_path are unchanged. The migration is new relative to origin/main, so no published checksum moves. A transactional command with no deadlineMs can still wait on the audit chain with no time limit.
findings.required_change: None for this PR. In the release notes or TransactionalCommand docs, state that lockTimeoutMs bounds only idempotency-key contention and that audit-chain waits are bounded by deadlineMs/statement_timeout.

summary: HEAD 3c1c3408 has exactly one marker, b647f568 'chore(repo): version 1.5.0 final release'. After the marker there are only two DEVAI Architect commits: bfa5d2a9 adds the FORBID-PUBLISH@5dffc830 receipt in law/policy, and 3c1c3408 changes only a work/ prompt. The marker moves 44 public manifests from 1.5.0-rc.3 to 1.5.0. The root manifest goes to 1.5.0, as the contract requires. All other private versions match origin/main, including 2.0.3-stynx.1. The marker consumes the 10 changesets and removes pre.json, and changeset status is empty. The audit lock_timeout fix is sound and does not change RLS or DDL boundaries. The PostgreSQL test is meaningful: it observes the reservation INSERT blocked on the advisory lock, holds the lock more than twice the 120 ms lockTimeoutMs, and requires a 201 with one handler invocation. The socket-DSN handling does not depend on the host. The Redis fixture now ties its controlled clock to real time, so EXPIREAT no longer deletes fixtures before the idle-expiry logic runs. I did not rerun the gates. The CI, release, trace and receipt PASS results come from the supplied logs, and I found nothing that contradicts them. The remaining OFS sensor gaps are proof-depth only, and the source conforms. The single final PR may be opened.
